source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 4ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Αφροδίσιος, Μίσδας, Μακρόβιος, Ουαλεριανός, Λεόντιος, Αντωνίνος οι Μάρτυρες και οι συν αυτοίς εν Σκυθουπόλει (Συρίας) μαρτυρησάντων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 4 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **This is a company the page enumerates by name — six head lines, six names — so it is six folders**, of which five are new here and the sixth, Valerian, is an upgrade on the corpus's existing `valerian-4-may`; «οι συν αυτοίς» names nobody further and nothing is claimed for the rest. **He is not the corpus's `aphrodisius`**, and the two are easy to separate: that folder is kept by the Romanian calendar on **21 June**, he is of **Cilicia**, he was tried by a ruler named **Dionysius**, and he was killed by a cut stone that fifty-five soldiers had lifted; this man is of **Scythopolis in Syria** on **4 May**, he came before his governor of his own accord, and he was stoned and clubbed with five named companions. Different day, different place, different story. **The page's couplets name a seventh man the listing does not**: one is headed «Eις τον Λεόντιον, Aντωνίνον και Mέλη» and reads «O Λεόντιος και συναθληταί δύω», Leontius and two fellow-contenders — so the verses know a Μέλης beside Leontius and Antoninus, and the listing and the head lines do not. **No folder was made for him**, because nothing on the page states that he is a person rather than a common noun, and the discrepancy is recorded here. No year, no emperor, no hymn, no relic; the synaxis was kept at the apostoleion of James the Brother of God inside the house of the Mother of God at the Chalkoprateia.
